clue.text: Very surprised when the beginning actually came first

parts.note: the beginning of something is its start
to have come first in a race is to have led

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished to find that the opening part really did arrive ahead of everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: To be startled is to be given a sudden shock or fright.

clue.text: Resign in order to become an entertainer

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Someone quits their job so they can go on the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A vocalist who performs songs is one kind of entertainer.

clue.text: I dream badly, love

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are poorly arranged and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sleeper confesses to a terrible dream, addressing a sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to regard them with warm approval, close to loving them.

clue.text: Try the underground for an experiment

definitions.note: the definition is adjectival, describing what the glass vessel is used for

parts.note: to try something is to test it
the Tube is the popular name for the London Underground railway

explanation.surface: A suggestion to sample the metro system as a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's underground railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender glass vessel closed at one end is the classic laboratory container used in experiments.

clue.text: The Spanish kiss is not for animals

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for 'the'

indicators.note: the word not says the following word is absent from what precedes it, so those letters are dropped

explanation.surface: A Spanish embrace is not intended for beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Elks are large deer, so they are animals by example.

clue.text: The Spanish weapons found at arms' centres

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for 'the'
bows are weapons that fire arrows

explanation.surface: Spanish arms are discovered in the middle of a gathering of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint halfway along each human arm is the elbow.

clue.text: Left, for example, to finish the story

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example
to finish is to end

explanation.surface: Something left as an example to round off a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional tale handed down, a story of uncertain truth.

clue.text: Do remote alteration to measuring device

indicators.note: an alteration changes something, here the order of the letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to modify a gauge from a distance.
explanation.definitionFit: An odometer is an instrument in a vehicle recording distance travelled.

clue.text: Demesnes cultivated by gardeners

indicators.note: cultivating land turns it over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Estates tilled by horticultural workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedsmen raise and sell seeds, so they are growers or gardeners.

clue.text: Am as keen as can be to have the same designation

indicators.note: the phrase suggests the letters taking whatever form they can, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone declares themselves as eager as possible to share a title.
explanation.definitionFit: A person bearing an identical name to another is called by the same name, so the definition describes that shared label.

clue.text: Take no notice of anyone partly foreign or exotic

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instruction to disregard anybody who seems at all alien or strange.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay no attention to someone is to disregard them, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Picture of red wine and fish

parts.note: port is a fortified red wine from Portugal
a ray is a flat sea fish

explanation.surface: A painting showing a glass of claret and some seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray is to depict or represent, as a verb meaning to picture.

clue.text: Mistakes made by deserter were caught in time

indicators.note: the deserter is said to be trapped inside the period of time, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is one who deserts, as rats are said to leave a sinking ship

explanation.surface: Errors by a runaway soldier came to light just before it was too late.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata is the Latin plural used for a list of printing errors or slips.

clue.text: Metal workers sink in mud up to a point

definitions.text: sink in mud up to a point

explanation.surface: Iron casters get bogged down partway in the mire.
explanation.definitionFit: Men who cast metal in a foundry work at that trade, and to founder is to get stuck or go down, as a horse in mire.

clue.text: Lady who should be in the pink

definitions.text: Lady who should be in the pink

parts.words: Lady who should be in the pink
parts.note: a woman's name that splits into two words describing a pale form of red, which is pink

explanation.surface: A woman who ought to be in fine health.
explanation.definitionFit: The name divides into words meaning a gentle red, which is what pink is.

clue.text: Green alcohol made in labs in the cellar

indicators.note: the drink is said to be produced inside the words that follow, so its letters lie within them

explanation.surface: Bootleg green liquor is brewed in laboratories down in the basement.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinth is a strong anise-flavoured spirit, famously green in colour.

clue.text: Only water

explanation.definitionFit: Mere means nothing more than, as in a slight amount, and a mere is also a small lake or pond.

clue.text: Tell everyone that the girl is overweight!

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another means it sits above, so it comes first

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
an ounce is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Broadcasting the news that a young woman is too heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce is to proclaim or make public, informing all.

clue.text: Even study the way of a worker

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn
St is the abbreviation for street, a way
the worker ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: Examine steadily how a labourer goes about the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Constant means unvarying or uniform, as even does of a rate or pace.

clue.text: Big glass boat

explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a large drinking glass for sherry or beer, and also a sailing vessel with two or more masts.

clue.text: The middle of the day whichever way you look at it

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: the phrase says the word reads identically in either direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Midday stays midday, whatever angle you consider it from.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve o'clock in the daytime is the midpoint of the day.

clue.text: Forward some money

explanation.definitionFit: To move forward is to progress, and a sum paid ahead of time, such as a loan on wages, is also so called.

clue.text: Sweet cryptic clue in the DAILY TELEGRAPH

indicators.note: the word in places the rearranged letters within the newspaper's initials

parts.note: DT is the short form of the newspaper's name

indicators.note: cryptic means obscure, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A nice puzzle appearing in the newspaper where this crossword is printed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' rearranges CLUE to ULCE, which goes 'in' DT.
explanation.definitionFit: Dulcet describes sweet and soothing sounds.

clue.text: Happy about the soldiers-they only looked fierce!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the happy word goes round the soldiers

parts.note: glad is a synonym of happy
RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Pleased about the troops' arrival, though they merely appeared threatening.
explanation.definitionFit: To glare is to stare angrily, so the definition is the past tense of that.

clue.text: Trails run in the back street

indicators.note: in puts the run inside the turned street abbreviation
back tells us to read the abbreviation the other way round

parts.note: a race is a run

explanation.surface: Footprints leading along a race through a rear alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ST into TS, and RACE goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Traces are marks or tracks left behind, like trails.

clue.text: Old student's better out of sight!

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil, and the 's adds S
someone made better after illness has been cured

explanation.surface: A former pupil has recovered and now cannot be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hidden from view has been concealed or covered over.

clue.text: May help to make a wave a big one

definitions.text: May help to make a wave

explanation.definitionFit: A hair curler is used to set curls, and a long heavy swell rolling in from the sea is also given this name.

clue.text: You might hear this again

parts.note: a sound that bounces back off a surface so it is heard a second time

explanation.definitionFit: A reflected sound repeats what was said, so it is heard once more.

clue.text: 17 short of no obscure shade

indicators.note: obscure suggests the remaining letters are muddled out of their order
being short of something means lacking it, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: the answer to 17 down, meaning tell everyone
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clue cross-referring to another, minus a negative, giving a murky colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of no' takes N and O out of ANNOUNCE, leaving ANUNCE, which 'obscure' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a subtle gradation, a fine shade of meaning or colour.

clue.text: Over 100 in crate — but not in the middle

indicators.note: over suggests the letters being turned over and jumbled together

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: More than a hundred items packed in a box, but none placed centrally.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram pool is C, IN and CRATE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Acentric is a technical word for lacking a centre or being off-centre.

clue.text: What is left of the property

explanation.definitionFit: A dead person's assets, bequeathed after death, form an estate, and a large house with its grounds is also so called.

clue.text: Make friends with Mac or Des

indicators.note: make tells us to form something new out of the letters given

explanation.surface: An invitation to befriend two men called Mac and Des.
explanation.definitionFit: Comrades are close companions or fellow members, like friends.
